title: Autoscaler undercounts warmup deadtime leading to reserved-pool shortfall during microbursts
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Production customers experienced transient but repeated dedicated pool capacity shortfalls during microburst traffic. The autoscaler was marking newly-leased nodes as immediately available despite a GPU/VM warmup deadtime (KV cache priming + driver slow-path) that prevents them from accepting real requests for a short window. This caused headroom to be overestimated, autoscaler to avoid additional scale-up, and downstream reserved-pool burst limits to be hit. Impact spans Hosted fallback usage and multiple Dedicated customers that rely on reserved pool burst credits.
impact: Customer-facing latency and 429s during short traffic spikes for ACME Health and ListCo; estimated 12-minute average window of degraded throughput per incident, SLA breaches for two customers, multiple support escalations. Internal: increased fallback routing to cheaper model variants and higher per-token cost while fallback active.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create dedicated reserved pool with normal warmup_deadtime telemetry disabled
2) Emit a microburst of parallel requests that exhaust headroom
3) Observe autoscaler leases nodes and immediately marks them available in allocation ledger
4) Verify through GPU metrics that KV cache priming and kernel JITs show no-ready state for ~30-90s while allocation ledger already schedules requests onto them
5) Repeat with patched controller that subtracts warmup_deadtime to confirm behavior changes
root_cause: A recent optimization (deferred_allocation v2) altered the lease lifecycle: lease 'ready' transitions were decoupled from node warmup signals to reduce perceived coldstart latency. In edge cases where warmup_deadtime > 0, the controller's headroom accounting used the lease-ready timestamp instead of the node-ready metric, causing a race where nodes were considered available earlier than they truly were.
mitigation_completed: 1) Immediate temporary mitigation: raised reserved-pool minimum headroom for impacted clusters (manual override) to force extra capacity while patch rolled out
2) Customer comms: sent incident notice to ACME Health + ListCo with short-term mitigation and ETA for patch
3) Fallback tuning: tightened fallback routing thresholds for Dedicated-to-Hosted fallbacks in affected regions
4) Enabled additional warmup telemetry dashboards (grafana link below)
ongoing_work: Implement fix in scale-controller to gate lease-ready -> allocation-ready transition on node-ready signal
Add unit + integration tests that simulate warmup_deadtime across heterogeneous GPU types
Canary rollout to 2 regions with extended microburst load harness
Postmortem and runbook updates (ownership handoff to capacity-sre)
proposed_fix: Patch: change lease lifecycle to require both 'lease-allocated' and 'node-ready' before incrementing available headroom. Add a safety window calibration per GPU type (warmup_deadtime_ms per instance-type) persisted in the cluster fingerprint store. Also add a fallback heuristic: if observed request failure rate spikes within 60s of node allocation, temporarily over-provision by N additional slots for that tenant class.
qa_plan: Unit tests for lease state machine, e2e harness injecting synthetic warmup delays, canary against non-critical tenants for 24h, monitor error rate, tail latency, headroom accounting metrics. Acceptance: no 5xx/429 regressions on canary and headroom metrics align with expected accounting within 1% under microbursts.
timeline: 2026-03-10: Incident detected and initial triage. 2026-03-11: Temporary headroom overrides applied; customer comms sent. 2026-03-12: Root cause identified and engineering PR started. 2026-03-14: PR opened and tests added; canary rollout scheduled. 2026-03-15: Canary rollout began in us-west-2. 2026-03-17: Target full rollout to all Dedicated clusters (subject to canary results).
rollback_plan: If the patch causes unexpected allocation regressions, revert the controller change via feature-flag flip; restore previous headroom overrides and set autoscaler to conservative scaling policy until stable. Run smoke tests to verify no extended preemption or double-allocation.

acceptance_criteria: Headroom accounting must never mark a node available before node-ready signal is observed
No customer-facing 429/5xx regressions in canary for 24h under synthetic microbursts
Automated test coverage added and passing in CI
Runbook updated and handoff completed to capacity-sre
postmortem_actions: Add warmup_deadtime calibration values for new GPU families
Include warmup readiness in autoscaler unit tests as part of CI gate
Document safe headroom defaults and provide a customer-visible advisory for Dedicated tenants about transient warmup windows
notes: This regression was introduced while optimizing perceived coldstart latency. Balancing perceived latency and actual readiness requires conservative accounting. The fix maintains low latency goals but ensures correctness for production bursts. Coordinate rollout with Dedicated account managers to avoid surprises for high-tier customers.
